newsitem.title: USA: Tax credits for college donations in Minn. bills.
newsitem.headline: Tax credits for college donations in Minn. bills.

text.p: Legislation that would give tax credits for donations to Minnesota colleges and universities was introduced in the state legislature Thursday, according to a news release from higher education groups in Minnesota.

The bills, introduced by Sen. John Hottinger, DFL-Mankato, and Rep. Gene Pelowski, DFL-Winona, would allow individuals to receive a tax credit of 50 percent of the amount of gifts to accredited public or private colleges and universities in Minnesota.
There would be a maximum credit of $500 for individuals and $1,000 for couples.

The proposed legislation would generate an estimated $6 million in credits in the first year, reflecting donations of more than $12 million to Minnesota colleges and universities, according to a news release.

"Tax credits have worked in other states to broaden the base of support for higher education," said University of Minnesota Foundation Chair Luella Goldberg, a supporter of the legislation. "The tax credit is an innovative public-private partnership to build needed support for colleges and universities, which are the lifeblood of our state's economy."
